requirement: IoT device profile model with @field_validator enforcing E.164 phone formatting with mode="before" pre-cleaning, strict SemVer 2.0.0 firmware with anchors, and lowercase normalized 64-hex fingerprint in mode="after".
skeleton: Pydantic v2 BaseModel with pre-compiled regex validators and mode-specific data sanitation.
caption: A pydantic v2 model for an IoT device profile whose three string fields are validated by pre-compiled regular expressions. PHONE_REGEX anchors an E.164 number: a plus sign, a leading digit from 1 to 9, and six to fourteen further digits, so a number of up to fifteen digits is accepted. SEMVER_REGEX is the full SemVer 2.0.0 grammar with anchors at both ends: three numeric components without leading zeros, an optional pre-release list after a hyphen, and optional build metadata after a plus sign. FINGERPRINT_REGEX accepts exactly sixty-four hexadecimal characters in either case. DeviceProfile sets extra to forbid and declares device_id, phone with max_length 16, firmware, and fingerprint. validate_phone runs in before mode as a classmethod: when the raw value is a string it first strips spaces, hyphens, and parentheses with re.sub, then requires a string that matches PHONE_REGEX with match, raising ValueError otherwise, and returns the cleaned value; because it runs before type validation, a formatted input with spaces and dashes is cleaned rather than rejected. validate_firmware runs in after mode and raises ValueError when the anchored SemVer pattern does not match, never substituting a default. validate_fingerprint runs in after mode, raises ValueError on a non-matching string, and returns the value lowercased so the same fingerprint written in upper case is stored identically. Every rejection surfaces as a pydantic ValidationError naming the field.

plan.intent: Validate and normalize an IoT device profile
constraints: A phone number is stripped of spaces, hyphens, and parentheses before it must match E.164, raising ValueError otherwise
Firmware must be a full SemVer 2.0.0 version, raising ValueError otherwise
A fingerprint must be 64 hexadecimal characters, raising ValueError otherwise, and is stored lowercase

rationale.teaches: Anchored regexes with match, a before-mode validator that cleans raw input, an after-mode validator that lowercases, and a validator that raises rather than substituting a default.
rationale.why: Regex validators fail open in quiet ways: a missing anchor accepts junk suffixes, search accepts embedded matches, and a substituted default hides bad input. Each has a payload that exposes it.

ops.docstring: Device profile whose phone, firmware, and fingerprint fields are checked by regex.

ops.stmt: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator

candidates.why_wrong: The SemVer regex is unanchored and applied with search, so a string like garbage1.2.3garbage validates.
The phone regex only allows 2 to 11 digits after the country code, so valid E.164 numbers with 12 to 15 digits are rejected.
The phone validator runs in after mode, so raw input with spaces or dashes fails type validation before it can be cleaned.
The fingerprint is not lowercased, so the same fingerprint in upper case is stored as a different value.
An invalid firmware string is replaced with 0.0.0 instead of raising, so bad input is silently accepted.
